In February 1869 Queen Ranavalona II of Madagascar and her husband, the prime minister Rainilaiarivony, were publicly baptised. Protestant Christianity became, in effect, the religion of the Merina state.

Missionaries of the London Missionary Society had arrived in 1818, welcomed by King Radama I, who wanted schools and Western skills. They set Malagasy in writing and translated the Bible. But Queen Ranavalona I saw Christianity as a threat to the ancestors and the monarchy. From 1835 she banned it and had many Christians killed.

Her successors reversed course. Ranavalona II went further: later in 1869 the royal idols, the sampy, were burned. Thousands of people followed the court into the churches, and stone churches were built in Antananarivo, including one at the Rova itself.

The conversion tied Madagascar more closely to Britain, but it did not save the kingdom: France conquered it in 1895 and ended the monarchy in 1897.
sum: In February 1869 Queen Ranavalona II of Madagascar and her husband, the prime minister Rainilaiarivony, were publicly baptised. Protestant Christianity became, in effect, the religion of the Merina state.
